NovaPharm Biotech Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaPharm Biotech Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaPharm Biotech Inc.'s financial results for the third quarter of 2023. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Robert Hayes, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter, CEO of NovaPharm Biotech Inc.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaPharm Biotech Inc. delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our oncology portfolio, label expansions across key franchises, and accelerating growth in emerging markets. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including pipeline advancements in antibody-drug conjugates and GLP-1 therapies, alongside disciplined execution in sales and marketing.

We are particularly excited about NovaADC-301 and its potential to become a best-in-class TROP2-targeted asset in HER2-low breast cancer, with topline data expected next year that could unlock over a billion dollars in peak sales.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Ramirez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results, including our updated guidance, geographic performance, marketing metrics, and regulatory milestones.

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thank you, Dr. Carter. As Dr. Carter mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $285 million, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 35% U.S. volume growth for our flagship PD-1 inhibitor, NovaLume, and initial contributions from our recently launched biosimilar to Keytruda, NovaPembrolizumab, which ramped to $45 million in its first full quarter post-FDA approval in June.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $50 million, or $0.85 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $75 million, or $1.20 per share.

Our operating expenses were $220 million, reflecting continued investments in R&D to support our pipeline while trending toward improved efficiency. We continue to invest in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $2.1 billion.

Let me now turn to our revenue guidance and the key upcoming catalysts that position NovaPharm for sustained growth in this dynamic pharma landscape. Our portfolio is anchored in high-margin oncology and rare disease franchises, with emerging momentum in GLP-1 agonists and next-gen ADCs—antibody-drug conjugates—amidst a market where global pharma revenues are projected to grow at 5-7% CAGR through 2028, per IQVIA estimates, driven by innovative modalities and label expansions.

First, on revenue guidance. For the full year 2023, we're raising our revenue outlook to $1.05 billion to $1.08 billion, up from our prior guide of $980 million to $1.02 billion. Looking to 2024, we're initiating guidance for net product revenues of $1.45 billion to $1.55 billion, representing 38-44% growth at the midpoint. Breaking this down: U.S. revenues are expected to comprise 65% of the total, or $940 million to $1.01 billion, driven by NovaLume's continued share gains in non-small cell lung cancer to 18% market share from 14% today—outpacing competitors in certain combo regimens per Symphony data—and full-year ramp of NovaPembrolizumab, targeting $250 million as payer access hits 85% formulary coverage by Q2.

Europe and ex-U.S. should deliver $350 million to $380 million, up 50% year-over-year, with EMA approval for NovaLume's frontline bladder cancer label expansion expected Q1 2024, unlocking €200 million in peak EU sales. We're also seeing early traction in Japan via our Shionogi partnership, where NovaLume volumes grew 40% quarter-over-quarter. Royalty and milestone streams are projected at $160 million to $170 million, including $50 million upfront from our recent out-licensing of the oral GLP-1 candidate, NovaSemide, to Eli Lilly for $300 million total potential milestones.

This guidance embeds a conservative 2-3% pricing pressure from the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare Part D redesign but is offset by our 15% gross-to-net adjustment improvement through optimized rebates and 340B carve-outs. OpEx as a percentage of revenue should trend down to 75-78% from 82% this year, supporting non-GAAP EPS of $2.85 to $3.15.

Shifting to key upcoming catalysts, which we view as de-risking our pipeline and driving multiple re-rating opportunities. We've bucketed these into near-term next 6-12 months and mid-term 12-24 months to give you a clear line of sight.

Near-term catalysts Q4 2023 through Q4 2024: PDUFA for NovaLume in MSI-high endometrial cancer in Q1 2024, with priority review granted by FDA after our Phase 3 EMBLAZE trial hit the primary endpoint of PFS with a 52% reduction in risk versus physician's choice, HR 0.48, p less than 0.0001. If approved, this adds a $400 million U.S. opportunity in a market underserved by current standards. Analysts model 20% approval probability baked in; we see 85% based on data.

Top-line readout from ENLIGHTEN-2 Phase 3 trial of NovaADC-301 in Q2 2024, our next-gen TROP2-targeted ADC in HER2-low breast cancer, enrolling 650 patients. Interim futility analysis cleared with 75% ORR; full data could position it as a best-in-class rival to leading assets, with projected $1.2 billion peak sales. This trial incorporates our proprietary linker technology, reducing payload off-target toxicity by 40% in preclinicals.

China NMPA approval and launch of NovaPembrolizumab in Q3 2024, bridging study success with bioequivalence to Keytruda; partnership with CSPC Pharma targets $150 million in Year 1 sales in a $2.5 billion import market, per IQVIA China. Interim data from NovaSemide Phase 2b in obesity in Q4 2024, oral small-molecule GLP-1 with 12% weight loss at 36 weeks versus 8% for benchmarks. Lilly's $100 million opt-in milestone triggers here, validating our platform amid the $100 billion GLP-1 market explosion.

Mid-term catalysts 2025 and beyond: BLA submission for NovaGene-45, our CRISPR-based CAR-T for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma in H1 2025. Phase 1/2 data showed 92% ORR with durable responses; RMAT designation accelerates path to $800 million peak in a post-commercial landscape. Strategic M&A or BD milestone: We're allocating $500 million from our cash position for bolt-on acquisitions in ADCs or gene therapies, similar to recent major deals. Expect 1-2 announcements in H1 2024.

Regionally, U.S. remains our growth engine at 40% CAGR, but we're diversifying: ex-U.S. now 30% of revenues, up from 22% in 2022, with Asia-Pacific growing fastest at 55% year-over-year on regulatory harmonization. Strategically, we're prioritizing portfolio expansions—like NovaLume's five labels in three years—while mitigating biosimilar erosion via innovation. Our R&D yield is top-quartile at 25% Phase 2 success rate versus industry 15%, per BIO stats. This guidance and catalyst slate support our journey to $3 billion in revenues by 2026, with oncology at 60% mix.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to reflect this momentum. Now, let's dive deeper into our geographic revenue breakdown, with a particular focus on the robust growth in emerging markets, underscoring our strategic pivot toward global diversification to mitigate U.S. pricing headwinds while capitalizing on underserved patient populations worldwide.

For Q3 2023, total net product revenues reached $285 million, up 28% year-over-year. U.S. revenues accounted for 64% of total net product sales, or approximately $182 million, representing a solid 12% year-over-year increase. This performance was driven primarily by our blockbuster oncology franchise, led by NovaLume, our anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody, which generated strong contributions despite a modest erosion in average selling price due to increased Part D rebate pressures under the Inflation Reduction Act. Volume growth more than offset this, fueled by label expansions into adjuvant settings for NSCLC and melanoma, following our supplemental BLA approval earlier this year. Our immunology portfolio contributed meaningfully, benefiting from strong uptake amid favorable payer mix shifts toward commercial coverage.

EMEA delivered 23% of revenues, or about $66 million, facing some FX headwinds from a strengthening USD but supported by volumes. Europe remains our second-largest market, with key countries comprising the bulk. Pricing remains challenged owing to HTA clawbacks and reference pricing harmonization under the EU HTA Regulation. However, volumes grew, supported by tender wins for NovaLume and the rollout of our CAR-T therapy in select markets post-EMA approval. We're actively managing gross-to-net adjustments here.

Asia-Pacific surged to 8% of total revenues, or $23 million—a standout 52% year-over-year growth. Ex-Japan APAC, which we classify as an emerging market cluster, drove much of this, up significantly year-over-year. China was the star performer, with contributions from NovaLume following NMPA approval and our first national tender inclusion under the NRDL reimbursement list. Volumes exploded, aided by our JV for local manufacturing, which reduced COGS and enabled faster market access. Japan added steady growth, bolstered by our partnership for co-promotion.

Latin America and other emerging markets rounded out at 5% of revenues, with strong growth. Brazil led with penetration via fast-track approvals, and India contributed on volume from patient access programs. These markets are seeing ASP stability for biologics, offset by volume potential from rising GDP per capita and universal healthcare expansions.

Zooming in on emerging market growth—which we define as ex-U.S./EU5/Japan, totaling 11% of revenues—this segment grew 55% year-over-year and now represents 25% of our total revenue growth delta. This isn't accidental; it's the result of targeted initiatives over the past 18 months: regulatory momentum with 12 new approvals across key regions since late 2022, including NCE designations in China for next-gen bispecifics; $250 million invested in regional capabilities, including new facilities to slash lead times by 40% and improve supply chain resilience; partnership ecosystem like our upfront deal with partners for Greater China rights to our ADC pipeline; and commercial innovation such as value-based pricing models and digital adherence platforms to boost persistency rates.

Looking ahead, we project emerging markets to grow at 40-50% CAGR through 2026, potentially reaching 20% of total revenues by then, driven by aging demographics, biologic uptake, and tailwinds from WHO essential medicines lists. Risks include FX volatility, tender pricing, and IP enforcement, but our hedging covering 70% of APAC exposures and patent thickets—averaging 15 years remaining—position us well. Our geographic mix is rebalancing toward high-growth emerging pockets while U.S. and EMEA provide stability. This diversification not only de-risks our P&L but enhances long-term shareholder value through optimized R&D allocation—now 40% of our pipeline trials include emerging market sites for faster enrollment and real-world evidence generation.

Moving to marketing and sales effectiveness metrics. In our industry, where peak sales for blockbusters can exceed $20 billion annually, optimizing marketing ROI is critical amid payer pressures, biosimilar erosion, and the shift to value-based contracting. Q3 demonstrated robust effectiveness across our portfolio, driven by our omnichannel strategy and data analytics investments.

Prescription metrics for NovaLume showed strong momentum. Total prescriptions grew 18% year-over-year to levels reflecting category outperformance per IQVIA data, with new Rx surging. This reflects targeted HCP detailing and increased share-of-voice via digital channels. Market share in NSCLC expanded, fueled by Phase III superiority data that triggered KOL endorsements.

On sales force effectiveness, our field reps achieved high call target coverage thanks to Veeva CRM integration with AI-driven optimization. Average scripts per rep improved, with top performers excelling. We're leveraging predictive tools, which boosted close rates on key targets. ROMI for NovaLume detailing spend stood well above our hurdle, generating significant incremental revenue.

Turning to digital and patient-centric initiatives—critical where many HCPs prefer virtual engagement—our patient support app saw strong downloads, driving adherence rates above industry norms. Website traffic to HCP portals grew, with solid email metrics converting to new Rx volume. We piloted AI chatbots for peer-to-peer exchange, reducing response times and lifting engagement scores.

Regionally, U.S. performance remains our powerhouse with strong NRx growth amid favorable reimbursement. Europe saw TRx expansion bolstered by HTA dossier wins via real-world evidence from our registry. In Asia-Pacific, we're scaling with recent approvals; NRx jumped significantly, capturing share versus competitors. Emerging markets contributed growth despite headwinds.

For our cardio franchise facing biosimilars, metrics held steady with solid ROMI via payer programs. Early data on next-gen assets shows strong ramp.

Strategically, we're doubling down on precision marketing. Q4 initiatives include closed-loop marketing for HCP journey mapping, targeting ROMI uplift, and enhancing AI/ML to predict payer shifts, especially with IRA price caps. Amid GLP-1 hype, we're reallocating budget to immuno-oncology storytelling.

Our marketing engine delivered strong revenue attribution from promo spend, versus industry average. This positions us for sustained NRx growth into 2025.

Finally, I'm thrilled to highlight our regulatory approvals and label expansions, standout areas this quarter. In a year where FDA issued over 50 novel approvals—up 15% from 2022—and EMA greenlit 42 new indications amid RWE scrutiny, we've punched above our weight. These milestones accelerant our peak sales trajectory across immunology, oncology, and rare disease franchises.

Our flagship PD-1/VEGF bispecific, NovaLume, secured FDA approval for frontline use in combination with chemo for high PD-L1 NSCLC patients, building on prior approval. Supported by Phase III trial with 682 patients, data showed 28% risk reduction in progression or death, HR 0.72, p less than 0.0001, with superior PFS, ORR, and DOR.

This catapults it into a large frontline market where combos capture growing share. Forecasting incremental U.S. peak sales, with competitive pricing. EMA approval followed under PRIME, unlocking EU potential. Filing with PMDA leveraging Breakthrough Designation.

Strategically, companion diagnostics ensure high adoption. For rare disease, our AAV9 gene therapy for SMA Type 2 got expanded label to ages 2-18, underpinned by Phase III showing motor improvements and survival benefits. Taps large opportunity versus peers, with J-code aiding uptake. EMA on track, NMPA discussions underway.

Technical enabler: RWE integration shaved review timelines per FDA guidance. In immunology, our IL-23 inhibitor got pediatric approval for psoriasis, meeting co-primaries in Phase III. Enters underserved segment.

EMA approved expansion of our BTK degrader to MZL, with strong ORR/CR in pretreated patients. These six approvals—across FDA, EMA, Health Canada—mark our most prolific year, with high Phase III success. Filed additional sNDAs.

US 60% of guidance, EU accelerating, APAC positioning for growth. Leaning into precision medicine: expansions tie to biomarkers commanding premiums. AI-enabled RWE investment de-risks more filings. Against peers, fortifies our moat with strong ROIC.

These wins drive organic growth, expanding addressable market significantly.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Dr. Carter.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thank you, John. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, good morning. Great quarter. On the emerging markets growth, particularly China and LATAM, can you talk more about how you're managing tender risks and FX there, and what gives you confidence in the 40-50% CAGR projection?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Good morning, David. Thanks for the question. On emerging markets, which contributed 55% YoY growth this quarter, our confidence stems from the initiatives we outlined: 12 approvals since late 2022, local infrastructure cutting lead times 40%, and partnerships like our China JV reducing COGS 15%. For tenders, we've won key NRDL inclusion in China, and in Brazil, value-based contracts tie to outcomes. FX is hedged 70% for APAC, and patent protection averages 15 years. Biologic penetration is low but rising with demographics, supporting that CAGR to 20% mix by 2026.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
To add, David, our pipeline trials now include 40% emerging sites for RWE, de-risking further.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel, JPMorgan:
Hi, thanks. On the regulatory side, congrats on the NovaLume frontline approval. How does this impact 2024 U.S. revenue specifically, and thoughts on competition from Keytruda combos?

Dr. Robert Hayes, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Lisa. The frontline NSCLC expansion for NovaLume in high PD-L1 patients addresses a $12 billion market, with our Phase III data showing superior PFS and ORR versus monotherapy standards. We're forecasting $450 million incremental U.S. peak by 2026, with Q1 launch at competitive WAC. Companion diagnostics with Foundation Medicine ensure 85% identification, driving adoption. Versus Keytruda, our bispecific profile positions us strongly in combos, as evidenced by Symphony share gains.

John Ramirez, CFO:
And Lisa, this flows into our raised 2024 guidance midpoint of $1.5 billion, with U.S. at 65%.

Operator:
Our next question is from Mike Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres, Morgan Stanley:
Morning, team. On marketing metrics, the ROMI improvement is impressive—can you expand on the AI tools driving sales force productivity and digital adherence, and any Q4 spend shifts?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Hi Mike. Our 112% call coverage and 4.2x ROMI on NovaLume reflect Veeva AI optimization and Salesforce Einstein for scripting, lifting close rates 22%. Patient app adherence hit 78% at 180 days via digital tools, and AI chatbots cut HCP response times 60%. Q4, 15% budget reallocation to immuno-oncology counters GLP-1 noise, with Komodo integration targeting 20% ROMI uplift via closed-loop marketing.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thanks, Mike. This positions NRx for 15-20% growth into 2025.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaPharm Biotech Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Key near-term catalysts: NovaLume MSI-high endometrial PDUFA Q1'24, NovaADC-301 topline Q2'24, NovaPembrolizumab China launch Q3'24, NovaSemide Phase 2b data Q4'24; mid-term: NovaGene-45 BLA H1'25, M&A H1'24. Targets $3B revenue by 2026.

Emerging markets projected 40-50% CAGR to 20% of total revenue by 2026, driven by 12 approvals, investments, partnerships.

Strong regional NRx/TRx growth; Q4 initiatives include closed-loop marketing and AI/ML for 20% ROMI uplift, reallocating 15% budget to immuno-oncology.

Recent NovaPembrolizumab FDA approval June; upcoming NovaLume MSI-high endometrial PDUFA Q1'24.
